title: `cov`: two-pass blocks with Chan merge; Welford when grouped on streaming
verdict: two-pass per block + Chan (in memory; streaming ungrouped); Welford (streaming grouped); no clamp; Decimal raises on streaming (PL-5)
description: `CovState` follows `var` (polars-var-std): two-pass per block of 128 merged by Chan's combine in memory, Welford's update in the streaming reducer. A weight at most `ddof` is null. `CovState` does not clamp.

Integers become doubles (`as f64`), so values above 2⁵³ round; decimals are cast to `Float64` in memory. The streaming engine checks for a primitive numeric type before it builds the reduction, and a decimal is not one: `cov` of a `Decimal` column raises `InvalidOperationError` on the default lazy engine and succeeds in memory.

Streaming, ungrouped, merges `moment::cov` per chunk, the block algorithm of the in-memory path; the per-value Welford update is the grouped streaming path. In memory a column of length 1 is taken as a broadcast constant, so the covariance of one pair is 0.0 with `ddof=0` and null with `ddof=1` without reaching `CovState`.
The docs are silent on a weight at most `ddof` giving NULL, the algorithm, the types `cov` takes and the engines: a docs gap.
No upstream test pins a `Decimal` input; it may change between versions.
reference: `AggFn.cov` (`covOf`) is two-pass: the two means, then the products of the deviations added in list order from +0.0, by n or n - 1. No pairs is NULL, and so is a sample of one pair. Engines may differ in the last bits (#54) until #85 bounds the error.

evidence.note: in memory: a length-1 side is a broadcast constant (cov 0.0 or null, corr NaN); else `CovState`/`PearsonState` per chunk pair, merged by `combine`
in memory: `Int32`, `Int64`, `UInt32`, `UInt64` (and `UInt64` for cov) read `as f64`; other types, decimals among them, cast to `Float64`
result type: the inputs' float supertype, else `Float64`
`CovState`, `PearsonState`: two-pass blocks, Welford's `insert_one`, Chan's `combine`
`cov`, `pearson_corr`: pairs with both values valid, `as_()` `f64`, blocks of 128
streaming `new_cov_reduction`: `polars_ensure!(dtype.is_primitive_numeric())`, which a decimal is not
streaming: `update_group` casts to `Float64` and merges `moment::cov` per chunk (ungrouped); `update_groups_while_evicting` uses `insert_one` per row (grouped)
streaming `new_pearson_corr_reduction`: the same primitive-numeric check
streaming corr finish: null at weight 0, else `PearsonState::finalize`
`is_primitive_numeric`: float or integer
ungrouped `cov`/`corr` lower to a streaming reduction
grouped `cov`/`corr` lower to a streaming reduction

notes: Confirms the null for a weight at most `ddof` on both engines. No test at py-2.1.0 runs `cov` or `corr` of a `Decimal` column on the streaming engine, so PL-5 has no test either way.

Polars's CI runs the unit tests by default, where a lazy `collect()` without `engine` runs the streaming engine (also once with `POLARS_IDEAL_MORSEL_SIZE=4`), and again with `POLARS_ENGINE_AFFINITY=in-memory` (.github/workflows/test-python.yml#L55-L78, #L168-L178); eager `Series` and `DataFrame` calls run in memory. Read at tag py-2.1.0 (commit 7f902bd3), not run.

Confirms PL-5 on the streaming engine: `cov` of two `Decimal(10, 2)` columns raises `InvalidOperationError` (`cov` operation not supported for dtype `decimal[10,2]`), where memory gives 2.625 (and `corr` 0.9707253433941508).

`python -m sverify_dev.probe_polars --diff --write` runs each observation (`STREAMING_OBSERVATIONS`, python/tools/sverify_dev/probe_polars.py) with `collect(engine='in-memory')` and `collect(engine='streaming')` and records both results. Polars 2.1.0 (Python), macOS arm64.
